name: Deep In-the-Money Buy-Write
summary: Buy shares and sell a deep ITM call (0.85+ delta) for a tiny, bond-like return; risk-equivalent to a short put and mostly a bad idea for an automated account.
max_profit: extrinsic value captured only, typically 0.2-0.5% of notional
max_loss: (share price - credit) x 100 - full downside below the strike with almost no upside
when_to_use: Rarely. Historically used to park cash at a small premium or to capture a mispriced deep call. Risk-identical to selling a cash-secured put at the same strike but with more commissions, more assignment exposure and worse fills. FLAGGED: generally a bad idea - prefer the equivalent cash-secured put.
entry_rules: Only enable if the equivalent short put at the same strike/expiry is NOT available or is priced worse after fees.
Require extrinsic captured >= 0.25% of notional; reject below that.
Require IV Rank >= 40 - there is no point at low vol.
management_rules: There is nothing to manage but assignment; monitor extrinsic every minute.
Close the unit as soon as 70% of the extrinsic is captured.
exit_rules: HARD: unwind the entire unit as one combo when extrinsic < 0.05 or by 15:30 ET on expiration day, whichever comes first.
Unwind before any ex-dividend date: a deep ITM call is almost always exercised into a dividend.
assignment_risk: Extreme. Deep ITM short calls are assigned early as a matter of routine, especially into dividends. This is the single highest-assignment-probability structure in the family.
buying_power: Shares in full; the credit offsets most of the cost.
liquidity_needs: Deep ITM options are thin and wide; require spread <= 0.10 absolute or skip.
common_mistakes: Believing the high credit means high income - it is almost all intrinsic. Taking full downside risk for a 0.3% return.
zero_dte_notes: Not usable - zero extrinsic to capture and guaranteed assignment.
family: Stock/ETF Shares Combined With Options (covered writes, protective hedges, collars, synthetics, repairs, conversions)
